subs.label: Crime & Thriller Series
subs.axis: Axis: by the series' engine, from who investigates (police, detectives, sleuths, lawyers), to who commits the crime (gangs, dealers, crews, antiheroes, real criminals), to what threatens the protagonist (killers, minds, households, avengers, agents, states, games)

leaves.label: Police Procedural
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the investigation itself: detectives, agents or a specialist unit work cases through interviews, evidence and chain of command, usually one case per episode (Law & Order, NCIS, Criminal Minds, Cold Case). A series about the lives of uniformed cops or of bent and undercover officers goes to B7-2; a two-hander built on the partnership to B7-3; a lab-led show to B7-4; a single literary detective to B7-9; a serialised single murder to B7-8.
leaves.aliases: cop show; police drama; keiji dorama
leaves.see: B7-2 Police Drama; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series; B7-4 Forensic Procedural; B7-8 Whodunit
leaves.axis: by the unit the series follows: detective squads, federal and specialist units, profilers, cold-case teams, then fantastic-premise procedurals last

leaves.label: Police Drama
leaves.defn: A series about the working lives of police officers themselves, the shift, the station, the street and the temptations of the badge, rather than about solving a case (Hill Street Blues, The Bill, The Shield, Line of Duty). A case-driven investigation series goes to B7-1.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series
leaves.axis: by the officers' world: patrol and precinct ensembles, then undercover and police-corruption dramas

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Series
leaves.defn: A police or law-enforcement series whose engine is a mismatched pair of partners whose friction drives the cases (Starsky & Hutch, Miami Vice, Castle, Rizzoli & Isles). An ensemble squad goes to B7-1; a sitcom about cops goes to B8.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth; B8 Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by who makes up the pair: two cops, a cop and a civilian or animal, then comic buddy cops

leaves.label: Forensic Procedural
leaves.defn: A crime series in which the lab, autopsy table or crime scene is the investigative engine and the leads are scientists, pathologists or coroners (CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, Quincy, M.E., Silent Witness, Unnatural). A squad drama that merely uses forensics stays in B7-1.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural
leaves.axis: by the forensic seat: crime-scene labs, then pathologists and coroners

leaves.label: Country Noir
leaves.defn: A crime series set in a rural, small-town, frontier or outback community where the land, isolation and local kinship shape the crime and the lawman (Justified, Longmire, Mystery Road, Happy Valley). A Scandinavian series goes to B7-6; a Scottish one to B7-7.
leaves.aliases: rural noir; outback noir; neo-Western crime
leaves.see: B7-6 Nordic Noir; B7-7 Tartan Noir; A10 Western
leaves.axis: by the terrain: American backcountry and frontier, outback and antipodean bush, then British, Irish and European countryside

leaves.label: Nordic Noir
leaves.defn: Scandinavian and Nordic crime drama in the bleak, socially critical register named for the cycle that followed The Killing and The Bridge: slow serialised investigations, damaged detectives, wintry landscapes (Wallander, Trapped, The Chestnut Man). Remakes and imitations set elsewhere stay with B7-1 or B7-8.
leaves.see: B7-7 Tartan Noir; B7-5 Country Noir
leaves.axis: by the shape of the investigation: serialised single-case runs, then recurring detectives with many cases

leaves.label: Tartan Noir
leaves.defn: Scottish crime drama in the Tartan noir tradition of Ian Rankin and Val McDermid: hard-edged detectives in Edinburgh, Glasgow or the islands (Rebus, Shetland, Karen Pirie). An English village mystery goes to B7-11.
leaves.see: B7-6 Nordic Noir; B7-9 Detective Drama

leaves.label: Whodunit
leaves.defn: A serialised mystery in which a single murder or disappearance, and the circle of suspects around it, sustains a whole season and the question who did it is the engine (Broadchurch, Mare of Easttown, And Then There Were None, Magpie Murders). A recurring detective solving a new case each story goes to B7-9.
leaves.see: B7-9 Detective Drama; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by who carries the mystery: police-led serialised investigations, then closed-circle and Golden Age adaptations, then ensemble and anthology whodunits

leaves.label: Detective Drama
leaves.defn: A series built around a single named detective of literary pedigree, police or private, who solves a self-contained case each story through deduction and character (Agatha Christie's Poirot, Inspector Morse, Sherlock, Galileo). A squad procedural goes to B7-1; a cosy village mystery to B7-11; a period-set detective to B7-12.
leaves.see: B7-11 Cozy Mystery; B7-12 Historical Mystery; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth
leaves.axis: by the detective's lineage: Sherlock Holmes and Holmesian geniuses, Golden Age sleuths, the novelists' police inspectors, then puzzle-mystery (honkaku) series

leaves.label: Inverted Detective Story
leaves.defn: A mystery series in which the audience sees the crime and culprit first and the pleasure is watching the detective work it out (Columbo, Poker Face, Elsbeth).
leaves.see: B7-9 Detective Drama

leaves.label: Cozy Mystery
leaves.defn: A gentle murder mystery set in a village, resort or closed community where violence happens offstage and charm, humour and a returning cast matter as much as the puzzle (Midsomer Murders, Murder, She Wrote, Death in Paradise, Father Brown). A period setting first goes to B7-12.
leaves.see: B7-12 Historical Mystery; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth
leaves.axis: by who solves the murders: village and island police, then amateur and clerical sleuths

leaves.label: Historical Mystery
leaves.defn: A detective or police series whose cases are set in a past era that shapes method and motive (Cadfael, Murdoch Mysteries, Foyle's War, Babylon Berlin). Period gangland sagas go to B7-16.
leaves.see: B7-9 Detective Drama; B7-11 Cozy Mystery; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era: medieval to Victorian, then the Edwardian and interwar years, then wartime and postwar decades

leaves.label: Amateur Sleuth
leaves.defn: A series in which a non-police investigator, a consultant, academic, doctor, writer or hobbyist, solves crimes through a special gift, usually alongside the police (Monk, Psych, The Mentalist, Only Murders in the Building). Licensed private investigators go to B7-14.
leaves.see: B7-14 Private Eye; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series
leaves.axis: by the sleuth's gift: specialist consultants to the police, then hobbyists and accidental sleuths, then comic sleuthing

leaves.label: Private Eye
leaves.defn: A series following a licensed private investigator or agency taking clients' cases, from hardboiled loners to glamorous agency teams (The Rockford Files, Magnum, P.I., Strike, Veronica Mars).
leaves.see: B7-13 Amateur Sleuth; B7-19 Neo-Noir
leaves.axis: by the eye's register: hardboiled loners, then glamour and action agencies

leaves.label: Legal Thriller
leaves.defn: A series in which a criminal trial, defence or prosecution is the suspense engine: lawyers, defendants and judges racing to the verdict (Perry Mason, The Night Of, How to Get Away with Murder, Presumed Innocent). Workplace legal dramas without the crime engine go to B1.
leaves.see: B1 Drama Series; B7-1 Police Procedural
leaves.axis: by whose side the story takes: defence lawyers, then the accused and their families, then judges and prosecutors

leaves.label: Gangster Drama
leaves.defn: A saga told from inside a criminal organisation, mob family or gang, its loyalties, succession and turf wars (The Sopranos, Peaky Blinders, Gomorrah, Sons of Anarchy). A series about the drug trade itself goes to B7-17.
leaves.aliases: mob drama; mafia saga; yakuza drama
leaves.see: B7-17 Narco Series; B7-21 True Crime Drama
leaves.axis: by the organisation: Mafia and mob families, period gangland, modern city syndicates and crews, outlaw biker clubs, then yakuza and Asian syndicates

leaves.label: Narco Series
leaves.defn: A series about the drug trade as an economy: cooks, dealers, cartels, smugglers and the agents chasing them (Breaking Bad, Snowfall, Queen of the South, ZeroZeroZero). A mob saga where drugs are one racket goes to B7-16; a dramatised real kingpin to B7-21.
leaves.see: B7-16 Gangster Drama; B7-21 True Crime Drama
leaves.axis: by the rung of the trade: cartels and trafficking routes, then street dealing and urban drug wars, then outsiders who become dealers

leaves.label: Heist & Caper
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the plan: a crew assembled for a robbery, a con or a theft, with the pleasure in the scheme and the double-cross (Money Heist, Hustle, Leverage, Lupin).
leaves.aliases: heist series; con-artist drama; grifter show
leaves.see: B7-19 Neo-Noir; B7-32 Death Game
leaves.axis: by the scheme: robbery heists, then cons and grifts, then gentleman thieves, then gambling

leaves.label: Neo-Noir
leaves.defn: A crime series told from the side of the morally compromised: fixers, hitmen, small-time crooks and ordinary people who slide into crime, in the fatalistic noir register (Better Call Saul, Ray Donovan, Good Girls, Mr Inbetween). An organised family saga goes to B7-16; a drug saga to B7-17.
leaves.see: B7-16 Gangster Drama; B7-17 Narco Series; B7-5 Country Noir
leaves.axis: by the antihero: ordinary people turned criminal, then fixers, lawyers and middlemen, then hitmen and assassins, then social-realist and anthology noir

leaves.label: Prison Drama
leaves.defn: A series set inside a prison, where incarceration, inmate hierarchies and escape are the engine (Oz, Wentworth, Prison Break, Locked Up).
leaves.see: B7-27 Action Thriller

leaves.label: True Crime Drama
leaves.defn: A scripted dramatisation of a real crime, case or criminal, told with named real people (American Crime Story, Des, Narcos, Scam 1992). Documentary series go to B11.
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B7-22 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the crime: murders and serial killers, then fraud and scandal, then robbery, then gangsters and drug lords, then terror and state crimes, then wrongful accusation and justice

leaves.label: Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.defn: A series organised around a serial killer, whether hunted across a season or followed from the inside (Dexter, The Following, You, The Fall). Episodic profiler units go to B7-1; real killers to B7-21.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-21 True Crime Drama; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by point of view: the killer's own story, then the hunt for the killer

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose suspense lies in the mind: obsession, manipulation, unreliable memory, a missing person or a community's hidden secret, rather than in action (Fool Me Once, Behind Her Eyes, The Missing, Sharp Objects). A thriller of marriage and household goes to B7-24.
leaves.see: B7-24 Domestic Noir; B7-8 Whodunit; B7-22 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the source of dread: a missing person or abduction, obsession and manipulation, identity and memory, a small community's buried secret, then time-slip and uncanny thrillers last

leaves.label: Domestic Noir
leaves.defn: A thriller set in marriage, family and the home, where the danger is a spouse, a lover, a neighbour or one's own household (Big Little Lies, The Undoing, Doctor Foster, Mine). An affair thriller led by sex goes to B7-25.
leaves.see: B7-25 Erotic Thriller; B7-23 Psychological Thriller; B1 Drama Series
leaves.axis: by where the threat sits: the spouse, then the family and its heirs, then the social clique, then neighbours and strangers in the home

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which sexual obsession or seduction drives the danger (Fatal Attraction, Dark Desire, Toy Boy). A marriage thriller without the erotic engine goes to B7-24.
leaves.see: B7-24 Domestic Noir; A15 Erotic Film

leaves.label: Revenge & Vigilante Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is justice taken outside the law: a wronged person's long revenge or a vigilante crew punishing those the system lets go (The Glory, Taxi Driver, The Equalizer, Vigilante).
leaves.see: B7-27 Action Thriller; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by who takes justice: vigilantes and avengers-for-hire, then a single wronged person's revenge

leaves.label: Action Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller driven by pursuit, combat and the ticking clock: counter-terror agents, lone ex-soldiers, bodyguards, hijacks and fugitives (24, Reacher, Bodyguard, The Fugitive). A spy story goes to B7-28.
leaves.see: B7-28 Espionage; B7-26 Revenge & Vigilante Thriller; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the mission: counter-terror and the ticking clock, lone heroes and ex-soldiers, bodyguards and protectors, hijacks hostages and sieges, then fugitives on the run

leaves.label: Espionage
leaves.defn: A series about spies, intelligence agencies, double agents and covert operations (Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, The Americans, Homeland, Slow Horses). Counter-terror action without tradecraft goes to B7-27.
leaves.see: B7-27 Action Thriller; B7-29 Political Thriller
leaves.axis: by the spy's world: Cold War tradecraft, period and wartime espionage, present-day agencies and counter-terror, gadget spy-fi, action spies and assassins, then spy comedy and secret double lives

leaves.label: Political Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller set in the machinery of state: governments, coups, diplomats, scandals and the press that exposes them (A Very British Coup, State of Play, Occupied, The Diplomat). A plot by hidden powers outside the state goes to B7-30.
leaves.see: B7-30 Conspiracy Thriller; B7-28 Espionage

leaves.label: Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which an ordinary person or a small group uncovers a hidden plot by corporations, cults or shadow powers (Rubicon, Utopia, The Capture, Hunters).
leaves.see: B7-29 Political Thriller; B7-31 Techno-Thriller
leaves.axis: by the hidden power: corporations and finance, then the state and its security services, then cults and secret societies, then science and medicine

leaves.label: Techno-Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which hacking, surveillance, AI or advanced technology is the engine of threat and solution (Mr. Robot, Person of Interest, Hackerville, Zero Day).
leaves.see: B7-30 Conspiracy Thriller; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Death Game
leaves.defn: A thriller in which participants are forced into a deadly or ruinous game with prizes and eliminations (Squid Game, Alice in Borderland, Liar Game, Kakegurui).
leaves.see: B7-18 Heist & Caper; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Teen Noir
leaves.defn: A mystery or thriller centred on teenagers, schools and campuses, where adolescent secrets, cliques and a death drive the plot (Pretty Little Liars, Veronica Mars, Riverdale, Girl from Nowhere).
leaves.see: B1 Drama Series; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by the setting: high-school secrets and murders, then classroom and teacher thrillers, then boarding-school and campus mysteries

leaves.label: Survival Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which characters are stranded, trapped or hunted in a hostile place and must survive while a mystery unfolds (The Wilds, The Stranded, Persons Unknown, Jirisan).
leaves.see: B7-32 Death Game; B9 Speculative Series
